porbos.title: The Day of Dhu Qarad • On the Road to Khaybar • The Morning at Khaybar

blocks.1: Three nights before setting out for Khaybar, a morning came on the edge of Madinah. Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) himself told the story of that morning. The Prophet’s {{1}} milch camels were grazing in the pastures of Dhu Qarad. With them was his slave Rabah (RA). Salamah had gone that way that day with the horse of Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydillah (RA). At dawn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Fazari attacked with his band. He killed one of the herdsmen. He began driving off the herd of camels. Salamah (RA) said to Rabah, take this horse to Talhah. Tell the Prophet {{2}} that the polytheists have taken his camels. He himself stood up on a hill. Facing Madinah he cried out three times, Ya sabahah! Morning calamity, help! Then he ran alone after the raiders. He was shooting arrows and chanting,
blocks.3: I am the son of al-Akwa‘; today is the day of the ruin of the base.{{1}}
blocks.4: Whoever he caught up with, the arrow would go through the saddle and straight up to the shoulder. Whenever someone turned around, Salamah would sit down at the foot of a tree and shoot that rider’s horse. When they entered a narrow mountain pass he would climb the mountain and chase them, hurling stones. In this way not one camel of the Prophet’s {{1}} remained in their hands. In their flight they left behind more than thirty cloaks and thirty spears. Salamah put a stone over each one as a mark, so that the Companions of the Prophet {{2}} might come and recognise them. They sat down in one place to eat breakfast. Salamah sat on top of a hill. The son of Badr al-Fazari said, who is that man? They said, he has not left our tail since dawn. He has snatched away everything we had in hand. He said, four of you go and catch him. Four got up and came. As soon as they came within earshot, Salamah (RA) said, do you know me? They said, no, who are you? He said, I am Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘. By the One who honoured Muhammad {{3}}, I can catch whichever of you I wish, and none of you can catch me. One said, I think so too. They turned back. Salamah did not leave his place. A little later, through the gaps in the trees, he saw the horsemen of the Prophet {{4}} coming. First of all, Akhram al-Asadi (RA). Behind him Abu Qatadah al-Ansari (RA), and further behind, Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (RA). Salamah caught Akhram’s horse by the rein. He said, Akhram, beware of them. Wait until the Prophet {{5}} and the Companions arrive. Akhram (RA) said, Salamah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day, and know that Paradise is true and Hell is true, then do not come between me and martyrdom. Salamah let go. Akhram and ‘Abd al-Rahman fought. Akhram cut the legs of ‘Abd al-Rahman’s horse; ‘Abd al-Rahman martyred Akhram with a spear and mounted his horse. Abu Qatadah went after him and finished him with a spear thrust. Even then Salamah did not stop. He had no horse; he ran on foot. So fast that behind him not even the dust of the Companions of the Prophet {{6}} could be seen any more. Before sunset he caught up with them near the spring of Dhu Qarad. They were thirsty, going down to drink water. Salamah drove them away from there; he did not let even a drop of water touch their mouths. He pierced one of them again with an arrow and said, take this, I am the son of al-Akwa‘, today is the day of the ruin of the base. The man cried out, may his mother weep for him! Are you that al-Akwa‘ who has been after us since dawn? Salamah said, yes, enemy of your own self, that very al-Akwa‘. In the evening when he reached the Prophet {{7}}, all the camels, spears and cloaks he had snatched back were in the hands of the Prophet {{8}}. Bilal (RA) had slaughtered one of those camels and was roasting its liver and hump for the Prophet {{9}}. Salamah said, O Messenger of Allah, let me pick a hundred men. I will pursue them and finish them all. Not one will be left to give news. The Prophet {{10}} smiled so that in the firelight his molars were visible. He said, Salamah, could you really do this? Salamah said, yes, by the One who has honoured you. The Prophet {{11}} said, now they have reached Ghatafan. There they are being entertained. In the morning the Prophet {{12}} said,
blocks.6: Today our best horseman is Abu Qatadah, and our best infantryman is Salamah.{{1}}
blocks.7: Then he gave Salamah two shares, the horseman’s share and the infantryman’s share, both together. On the way back to Madinah he seated him behind himself on the back of his she-camel al-‘Adba’. No horse, no companion. Yet the one who ran alone and brought back the whole herd, the Prophet {{1}} lifted up behind himself. We often think, what can I do alone? I have no manpower, no horse. Salamah did not think any of this. Before him there was just one matter: the camels belong to the Prophet {{2}}. The work was in front of him, so he went and caught it. He did not sit waiting for the rest to arrive. On the way back an Ansari began calling out, will anyone race me to Madinah? No one? Over and over, the same words. Salamah (RA) said, do you not respect even an honourable man? The man said, no, except the Messenger of Allah. Salamah said, O Messenger of Allah, my parents be sacrificed for you, let me get down. The Prophet {{3}} said, if you wish. Salamah got down and ran. He stayed a little behind for a hill or two, then he caught up with the man and, giving a slap between the shoulders, said, I’ve got you. The man said, so it seems. Salamah reached Madinah first. He did not get down without informing the one on whose camel he was sitting behind. Permission even before entering a race. By Allah, not even three nights had passed in Madinah when we set out with the Prophet {{4}} on the road to Khaybar, Salamah used to say.{{5}}
blocks.9: About a month and a half after returning from Hudaybiyah, at the beginning of the seventh year of Hijrah, the Prophet {{1}} set out toward Khaybar. It was the biggest fortress-city of the Jews, north of Madinah; the exiles of Banu al-Nadir had sat right there and built the alliance of the Confederates at the Trench. Only those who had been at Hudaybiyah went along.{{2}}
blocks.10: Those who had sat at home with excuses on the journey of Hudaybiyah also sensed it: Khaybar was ahead. Smelling the spoils, they wanted to go along. The Qur’an had said this beforehand in this way,
blocks.12: (O Muslims!) When you go to gather spoils of war, those who stayed behind (from the journey of Hudaybiyah) will say, let us go with you as well. They want to change the word of Allah. Tell them, you shall never come with us. Allah had said so before. Then they will say, in fact you bear envy toward us. No; rather they are such people that they understand very little of speech.{{1}}
blocks.13: Those who were not to be found on the journey of hardship are the very first on the journey of profit. We know such companions. Busy on the day of work, present on the day of sharing. Allah had made the account clear that very day: whoever was not in the hardship will not be in the fruit either. A night road. One of the caravan said, ‘Amir, won’t you recite some of your little verses for us! ‘Amir ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) was a poet. Coming down and driving the camels along he began to sing,
blocks.15: O Allah, if not for You we would not have found guidance, nor given charity, nor prayed. So forgive, we are ransomed for You; when we face the enemy keep our feet firm, and send down tranquillity upon us.{{1}}
blocks.16: The Prophet {{1}} asked, who is singing? The people said, ‘Amir. He said, may Allah have mercy on him. In the battle of Khaybar ‘Amir (RA) went to strike a Jew with his sword; the sword was short, it came back and hit his own knee. He was martyred from that very wound. People began to say, ‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted, he killed himself. On the way back the Prophet {{2}} took the hand of his nephew Salamah (RA) and asked, what is the matter? Salamah said, my parents be sacrificed for you, people are saying ‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.18: Whoever said this has said wrongly. For him there are two rewards; he was a hard worker, a mujahid in the way of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.19: What appeared from the outside was an accident. What was written with Allah was two rewards. The Prophet {{1}} did not pass judgement on the outcome of others’ deeds as easily as we do. Reaching the mouth of a valley on the way, the Companions, in joy, raised their voices in takbir: Allahu akbar! Allahu akbar! La ilaha illa Allah! The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.21: Be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling a deaf one, nor an absent one. You are calling One who is All-Hearing, very near, and He is with you.{{1}}
blocks.23: Moving toward a fortress-city. Voices heavy, chests swelling. Even at this moment the Prophet {{1}} reminded them that the One being called is not far away. There is no need to shout to make Him hear. We often make du‘a by raising a cry, as if Allah were somewhere far. Yet He is right with us. Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) was then behind the Prophet’s {{2}} mount. He was saying to himself, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. The Prophet {{3}} heard and called, ‘Abdullah ibn Qays! Abu Musa said, at your service, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet {{4}} said, shall I tell you a phrase from the treasure of Paradise? Abu Musa said, certainly, O Messenger of Allah, my parents be sacrificed for you. The Prophet {{5}} said,
blocks.25: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. This is one of the treasures of Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.26: The Companions were going on a journey of victory. And one of them was saying to himself the very phrase whose meaning is: I have no power, I have no strength, everything is Allah’s. The Prophet {{1}} called exactly that a treasure of Paradise. The nearer victory comes, the more tempting the thought of one’s own strength becomes. That phrase there is a rein.
blocks.28: He halted at a place called Sahba, very near Khaybar. After praying ‘Asr he asked for food. For the whole army only barley meal was found. Everyone mixed it in water and chewed it. The Prophet {{1}} rinsed his mouth, and so did the Companions. Then they prayed Maghrib.{{2}}
blocks.29: Those who were going toward a fortress-city had barley meal as their provisions. When we set out on a journey we lengthen the list of food. Their list was short, their goal big. At night they reached near Khaybar. On reaching a settlement by night, the Prophet {{1}} would not attack before morning. He would wait, keep listening; on hearing the adhan he would halt, and only if he did not hear it would he attack.{{2}}
blocks.30: In the morning the people of Khaybar came out to the fields with spades and baskets. Seeing the army in front of them they shouted, Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and his army! The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.32: Allahu akbar, Khaybar is ruined. When we descend on the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.{{1}}
blocks.33: Even on the night of war, a wait for an adhan. Where Allah’s name was uttered, the sword did not descend. Not striking merely because one has the power; first being sure on whom one is striking. Fortress after fortress fell. The fortress for which the banner of victory was placed in the hand of ‘Ali (RA), that story has been told before, in Dars 4. At Khaybar sixteen Muslims were martyred. Ninety-three Jews were killed.{{1}}
blocks.34: Fortress after fortress came into their hands. Fields, gardens, date groves. Those who had spent year after year in Madinah’s houses on dates and water; ‘A’ishah (RA) has told their words: when Khaybar was conquered we said, now we will eat dates to our fill.{{1}}
blocks.35: The nation that once thought eating dates to its fill was the fruit of victory, Allah then laid before it the keys of great empires. This promise the Qur’an had already announced, in two steps,
blocks.37: Allah has promised you abundant spoils, which you will seize. He has granted you this victory immediately and withheld the hands of people from you, so that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to the straight path. There is yet another victory, which has not so far come within your power, but Allah has kept it within His own grasp. Allah is fully able over all things.{{1}}
blocks.38: The immediate victory is Khaybar; and another victory, still beyond reach of power, but encircled by Allah’s hand. What is out of my reach today may fall into my hand tomorrow from inside Allah’s encirclement. We see only today’s account.

The ‘translation’ of ‘al-yawm yawm al-rudda‘’ is a free rendering. Timing: Salamah himself said, before three nights had passed we set out for Khaybar; the dars keeps this order of Muslim. We chewed it and ate. Then he asked for water and rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed ours. Then he prayed Maghrib, and did not make fresh wudu’.’ In Ahmad 15990, Arna’ut: the chain is sahih.

quiz.q: On the Day of Dhu Qarad, whom did the Prophet ﷺ call ‘our best horseman today’?
quiz.e: And the best infantryman was Salamah; Muslim 1807.

quiz.q: In which Hijri year did the Khaybar expedition take place?
o: The end of the sixth year
quiz.e: At the beginning of 7 AH, on returning from Hudaybiyah.

quiz.q: According to the note in Tawdih al-Qur’an, who received permission to go on the Khaybar expedition?
o: A special selected group of the Ansar
quiz.e: It is stated in the note on Surah al-Fath 48:15.

quiz.q: Who was driving the camels on the way to Khaybar, singing poetry?
quiz.e: ‘Amir ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA).

quiz.q: How was ‘Amir ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) martyred?
o: The stone wall of the fortress collapsed
His own sword came back and struck him
quiz.e: The sword was short; it came back and struck his own knee.

quiz.q: In reply to ‘‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted’, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: His matter is in Allah’s hand
He will not get the rank of a martyr
quiz.e: He said, whoever said this has said wrongly; for him are two rewards.

quiz.q: What is learned from the Prophet’s ﷺ reply about ‘Amir’s death?
o: There is no reward for death by accident
Reciting poetry is forbidden in war
The decision that no one with a short sword should go to war
No hasty judgement about the outcome of others’ deeds
quiz.e: Outwardly an accident; with Allah, two rewards.

quiz.q: After someone’s death people are making bad remarks about their deeds; what does this dars teach?
o: Not passing judgement by outward appearance
Informing their family of the matter
quiz.e: About ‘Amir the Prophet ﷺ said, whoever said so has said wrongly.

quiz.q: Not found on the journey of hardship, first present on the journey of profit; in which incident is this picture found?
o: Those left behind wanting to go along
The accident of ‘Amir’s sword and people’s verdict
The Prophet’s ﷺ joy on seeing Ja‘far
quiz.e: Al-Fath 48:15.

quiz.q: On reaching a settlement at night, what did the Prophet ﷺ do before attacking?
o: Raid stealthily in the very darkness of night
Wait for the adhan until morning
Send an envoy with a letter
quiz.e: On hearing the adhan he would refrain; only if he did not hear it would he attack.

quiz.q: What did the people of Khaybar come out with in the morning?
quiz.e: They had come out for work in the fields.

quiz.q: Seeing the people of Khaybar, which sentence did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Allah alone is our only helper
quiz.e: Allahu akbar, Khaybar is ruined.

quiz.q: What is the significance of waiting for the adhan even on a night of war?
o: No sword in a settlement of Allah’s name
Fighting at night is physically hard
A strategy of letting the enemy sleep
Giving the soldiers time to pray
quiz.e: Where the adhan is called, there is no attack.

porbos.title: The Measure of the Date Grove • The Poisoned Goat • Fadak, Wadi al-Qura and Tayma’ • Ja‘far Returns • Fajr on the Way Back

blocks.0: The Measure of the Date Grove
blocks.1: After the victory the Prophet {{1}} let the Jews of Khaybar remain on their own land. They would cultivate, half the crop theirs, half the Muslims’.{{2}}
blocks.2: When harvest time came, to fix the shares by estimating the quantity of the fruit, the Prophet {{1}} would send ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA). The Jews gathered the jewellery of their women and placed it before him; these are yours, lighten our share a little, give a little concession in the division. Ibn Rawahah (RA) said,
blocks.4: O Jews, among Allah’s creation you are the most disliked by me. Yet this dislike of mine for you will not drive me to be unjust to you. I have estimated twenty thousand wasq of dates; if you wish, take this share, and if you do not, I will take it.{{1}}
blocks.5: And he said, the bribe you are offering is forbidden; we do not eat it.{{1}}
blocks.6: The Jews said, it is on this very justice that the heavens and the earth stand. To be just with someone we dislike is the hardest thing. The heart wants to give a little less in the measure, to add a little more sting in speech. Ibn Rawahah (RA) did not hide the dislike, he said it with his own mouth; but he did not let its shadow fall on the scales.
blocks.8: At Khaybar a Jewish woman brought a cooked goat for the Prophet {{1}}. It was mixed with poison. The Prophet {{2}} put a piece in his mouth. The woman was brought in. The Companions said, shall we not kill her? The Prophet {{3}} said, no.{{4}}
blocks.9: He carried the pain of that poison for the rest of his life. In his final illness he said to ‘A’ishah (RA),
blocks.11: ‘A’ishah, I still feel the pain of the food I ate at Khaybar. Now it seems the vein of my heart is being cut by that poison.{{1}}
blocks.12: The one who had wanted to take his life, he did not punish that day for himself. The pain remained for four years, the revenge did not. One who can let go like this of a wrong done to himself, his forgiveness is no strategy; it is a nature.
blocks.14: The news of the conquest of Khaybar spread around. To the Jews of Fadak the Prophet {{1}} had earlier sent someone and given the call to Islam. They had delayed. This time, at the news of Khaybar’s fall, Allah poured fear into their hearts. They themselves sent a proposal of peace, just like Khaybar’s: half the year’s crop for the Muslims. The Prophet {{2}} accepted the proposal. Fadak had come into hand without any expedition, so it was not distributed as spoils of war. Its fifth too was not set apart. Fadak was the Prophet’s {{3}} designated property. After this the Prophet {{4}} went to Wadi al-Qura. A group of Jews lived there, with some Arabs. As soon as the Muslims dismounted they rained arrows on them. In the very first blow the Prophet’s {{5}} slave Mid‘am (RA) was martyred. The Prophet {{6}} arranged the army and again called them to Islam. They refused. One from their ranks came out and called for single combat. Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) went forward and finished him. A second came out, and Zubayr finished him too. Before the third went ‘Ali (RA). In this way eleven heroes fell one after another. Every time one was killed the Prophet {{7}} would call the rest again to Islam. When the time of prayer came the Prophet {{8}} would pray with the Companions. After the prayer, the call again. It went on like this until evening. The next morning when the Muslims attacked, before the sun had risen a spear’s length, everything in their hands had come into the hands of the Prophet {{9}}. Staying there four days he distributed the spoils. The land and the date palms he left in the hands of the Jews, on a sharecropping basis like Khaybar.{{10}}
blocks.15: Even on the busiest day the prayer did not stop. And right after the prayer, the call. In the midst of swords he did not let da‘wah get lost. The person who pushes prayer aside under pressure of work sees the account upside down. It is prayer that makes room for work. Meanwhile the Jews of Tayma’ saw: Khaybar was gone, Fadak was gone, Wadi al-Qura too was gone. Without any protest they themselves came with a proposal of peace. The Prophet {{1}} accepted. He sent them a letter, the gist of which: for them there is Allah’s protection, jizyah will be on them, no wrong will be done, no one will be exiled. The night is gentle, the day is harsh; that is, this agreement will always remain in force. The letter was written by Khalid ibn Sa‘id (RA).{{2}}
blocks.16: A paper of peace on a day of strength. In this letter it is written that no one will be taken out of his home. Those who had the power to break houses wrote out an agreement.
blocks.18: Khaybar had only just been conquered. Right then a boat party arrived; Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib (RA) and his companions were returning from Habashah. They had left Makkah about thirteen years earlier; they had never seen Madinah with their own eyes. With them was the group of Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA), come from Yemen, whose boat had been driven by a storm to Habashah.{{1}}
blocks.19: The Prophet {{1}} went forward. He embraced Ja‘far and kissed him on the forehead between the two eyes. Then he said,
blocks.21: By Allah, I do not know which I should be happier about: the conquest of Khaybar, or the arrival of Ja‘far.{{1}}
blocks.22: The conquest of a whole fortress-city, and one man’s return; he placed the two in the pans of a scale, then could not decide which was heavier. The brother he had not seen for thirteen years; on getting him back, even the joy of victory fades. The Prophet {{1}} gave Ja‘far’s companions a share too from the spoils of Khaybar. Though they had not been in the fight. Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) said, he gave a share to no one who was not present at the conquest; the exception was only us, the people of the boat.{{2}}
blocks.23: By the rule of accounts they should not have received a share. But those who had not simply stayed on the sidelines, who even from afar had left everything for the sake of faith, their account the Prophet {{1}} wrote with his own pen.
blocks.24: The People of the Two Hijrahs
blocks.25: Ja‘far’s wife Asma’ bint ‘Umays (RA) went one day to Hafsah (RA). ‘Umar (RA) came in and asked, who is this? Hafsah said, Asma’. ‘Umar said, oh, that Abyssinian one? The one of the sea? Then he said, in hijrah we are ahead of you; so we have more right over the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. Asma’ (RA) became angry. She said, by Allah, never. You were with the Messenger of Allah {{2}}; he fed your hungry and counselled your ignorant. And we were in a far-off strange land, among disliked people; all of it for Allah and His Messenger. Until I inform the Messenger of Allah {{3}} of your words, I will neither eat nor drink anything. When the Prophet {{4}} came, Asma’ (RA) told the whole matter. The Prophet {{5}} said,
blocks.27: He is not more entitled to me than you. For him and his companions there is one hijrah, and for you, the people of the boat, two hijrahs.{{1}}
blocks.28: Asma’ (RA) used to say, after this Abu Musa and the people of the boat would come to me in groups to hear this hadith. Nothing in the world was more joyful to them, nothing greater, than this. Those who had been far, out of sight, the Prophet {{1}} did not forget them; rather he doubled their account. Around us too there are such people, who have gone far for work, whose contact has lessened. Because they are not near, their right does not diminish.
blocks.30: A night on the way back from Khaybar. After travelling all night, when the party was tired, the Prophet {{1}} halted at a place. He said to Bilal (RA), keep watch for us over the night. Bilal prayed as much as he could. Everyone fell asleep. As Fajr drew near Bilal leaned against his camel and sat facing east. Tiredness won. His eyes closed. No one woke. The sun came and touched their bodies. First of all the Prophet {{2}} woke. In a start he called, Bilal! Bilal (RA) said,
blocks.32: O Messenger of Allah, my parents be sacrificed for you. The sleep that seized you has seized me.{{1}}
blocks.34: The Prophet {{1}} did not scold. He only said, pull the camels, let us move away. After going some distance he made wudu’, told Bilal to say the iqamah, and led Fajr in congregation. After the prayer he said,
blocks.36: Whoever forgets a prayer, let them pray it as soon as they remember.{{1}}
blocks.38: The one he gave the duty of keeping watch was the very one who fell asleep. In response came neither rebuke, nor question, nor fault-finding. Only the next thing to do: move away, make wudu’, pray. What to do after a mistake, that he taught. When a mistake happens we first look for the guilty. Who did it, why did they do it, how did they do it. Time slips out. The prayer that has been missed, pray that first, then the rest of the talk.

quiz.q: What agreement was made about the land of Khaybar?
o: All the land in the Muslims’ hands
Jizyah collected in place of the land
quiz.e: They would cultivate, and half the crop would be theirs.

quiz.q: Who was sent to estimate the crop of Khaybar?
quiz.e: ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA).

quiz.q: What did the Jews offer Ibn Rawahah?
quiz.e: They gathered the women’s jewellery and offered it as a bribe.

quiz.q: How many wasq of dates did Ibn Rawahah (RA) estimate in all?
quiz.e: Twenty thousand wasq.

quiz.q: Even after saying his dislike aloud, how did Ibn Rawahah (RA) keep justice?
o: He did not let the dislike influence the measure
He fixed the shares by taking the bribe
He had taken the entire share of the crop for his own side
quiz.e: He did not hide the dislike, but did not let its shadow fall on the scales.

quiz.q: Why did the Jews say, ‘on this the heavens and the earth stand’?
o: Pleased at his accepting the bribe
Because they got the whole crop themselves
Getting full justice even from an enemy
Compelled by fear of the Prophet ﷺ
quiz.e: Justice is the foundation of the heavens and the earth; they acknowledged it themselves.

quiz.q: I have sat down to settle accounts in a dealing with a person I dislike from the heart; which incident should I remember?
o: The scene of the morning at Khaybar
Ibn Rawahah’s estimating of the dates
The breaking of nine swords in Khalid’s hand
quiz.e: The dislike must not enter the measure.

quiz.q: Someone wants to give something in the name of a gift to get work done; what is the lesson of this dars?
o: There is no harm in accepting a small gift
Take it and return it later
It is enough to take it secretly, not in front of everyone
Call a bribe a bribe and return it
quiz.e: Ibn Rawahah said, this bribe is forbidden, we do not eat it.

quiz.q: When it was proposed to kill the woman who brought the poisoned goat, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
quiz.e: He said, no.

quiz.q: In his final illness, to whom did the Prophet ﷺ speak of the pain of the Khaybar food?
quiz.e: ‘A’ishah (RA).

quiz.q: What does not punishing the poisoner for himself indicate?
o: The poison was in fact not harmful
Forgiveness for a wrong done to oneself
quiz.e: The pain remained for four years, the revenge did not.

quiz.q: Someone has done me great harm, yet I have the power to take revenge; what is the example of the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Settling the score when the chance comes
quiz.e: He bore the pain of the poison and did not take revenge.

quiz.q: Which place came into hand without any expedition and so was not distributed as spoils?
quiz.e: Fadak was the Prophet’s ﷺ designated property.

quiz.q: What does the continuity of prayer and da‘wah at Wadi al-Qura teach?
o: Prayer and da‘wah even under pressure
The worth of a date is understood when it runs out
The right of those far away does not diminish
Not passing judgement by outward appearance
quiz.e: Every time one was killed, the call was made again.

quiz.q: From where had Ja‘far (RA) returned?
quiz.e: From Habashah, with a boat party.

quiz.q: Whose group had come with Ja‘far, whose boat had been driven by a storm to Habashah?
quiz.e: The group of Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA).

quiz.q: On getting Ja‘far back, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: I do not know which makes me happier
There is no day greater than Khaybar today
I was not waiting for your return
Now you will stay in Madinah
quiz.e: The conquest of Khaybar or Ja‘far’s arrival, I do not know which.

quiz.q: How many hijrahs did the Prophet ﷺ speak of for the people of the boat?
quiz.e: For you, the people of the boat, two hijrahs.

quiz.q: What is expressed in putting the conquest of Khaybar and Ja‘far’s arrival in one pan of the scale?
o: A brother’s worth equals a victory
The conquest of Khaybar was small
Ja‘far had taken part in the conquest
The Prophet ﷺ was not happy with the conquest of Khaybar
quiz.e: On getting his brother back after thirteen years, even the joy of victory fades.

quiz.q: Why did Asma’ (RA) become angry?
o: ‘Umar had called her by an insulting name
It makes the sacrifice of staying far away look small
Hafsah had not listened to her
quiz.e: ‘Umar had said, we are ahead in hijrah, so we have more right.

quiz.q: Why did the people of the boat come to Asma’ in groups to hear the hadith?
o: They wanted to write down the hadith
To complain to the Prophet ﷺ against ‘Umar
Nothing in the world was more joyful than this
quiz.e: Asma’ herself said, nothing was greater in their eyes than this.

quiz.q: Meeting an old friend after a long time; what does the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ teach?
o: Avoiding them by speaking of busyness
quiz.e: He embraced Ja‘far and kissed his forehead.

quiz.q: Someone speaks dismissively of the contribution of a brother who has gone far away for work; what does this dars say?
o: Those who are near have more right
Staying far does not diminish the right
quiz.e: The people of the boat have two hijrahs.

quiz.q: A relative living abroad has returned home; what welcome is closer to the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Sending word while sitting at home
Only asking after well-being on the phone
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ went forward and embraced Ja‘far.

quiz.q: What does the Prophet’s ﷺ behaviour with Bilal (RA) in the incident of the missed Fajr teach?
o: The right of those far away does not diminish
Justice even with those one dislikes
Showing what to do without finding fault
Allah is near even on the day of victory, this remembrance
quiz.e: Only: move away, make wudu’, pray.

quiz.q: Which is the example of showing what to do, without finding fault, when a mistake has happened?
o: Releasing the woman of the poisoned goat
Saying nothing to Bilal on the missed Fajr
Returning the jewellery of Ibn Rawahah’s bribe
The reply to those who said ‘‘Amir’s deeds are wasted’
quiz.e: Muslim 680.

porbos.title: ‘Umrat al-Qada’ • Mu’tah • The Three Hundred at the Seashore • Final Word

blocks.1: A year came around. In the month of Dhu al-Qa‘dah of the seventh year of Hijrah, the Prophet {{1}} went to Makkah to perform ‘umrah in accordance with the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. This ‘umrah is called ‘Umrat al-Qada’. All who had been at Hudaybiyah, the Prophet {{2}} asked to come along. Except those who had been martyred in the meantime, no one stayed behind. Two thousand people, not counting women and children. This time they did not enter with weapons. At a place called Yajaj they left all their arms under the guard of two hundred men. With them there was only the sheathed sword, just as it was written in the treaty.{{3}}
blocks.2: The polytheists of Makkah were looking from the direction of the mountain. They were saying among themselves, the fever of Yathrib has weakened them. The Prophet {{1}} said to the Companions, walk fast in the first three rounds, swaying the shoulders, so that the polytheists see your strength.{{2}}
blocks.3: That fast walk of the tawaf the pilgrims still do today. What began one day as the answer to an accusation of weakness remained a Sunnah until the Day of Resurrection. Showing the believer’s firmness too sometimes becomes worship. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) said, the Prophet {{1}} did not tell the Companions to do ramal in all the rounds, only out of compassion for them. Showing strength in the first three rounds, walking normally in the remaining four.{{2}}
blocks.4: The one at whose command the Companions would give their lives saw how tired the Companions were. Even inside the command to show strength there was a reckoning of capacity. ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) was walking ahead of the Prophet {{1}} reciting verses, addressing the disbelievers: clear the way. ‘Umar (RA) said, Ibn Rawahah, in front of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, in Allah’s Haram, poetry? The Prophet {{3}} said, ‘Umar, let him be; his words reach them faster than arrows.{{4}}
blocks.5: A year earlier ‘Umar (RA) had asked, did you not say we would go to the Ka‘bah and perform tawaf? That day the answer had come, did I say, this very year? Today is that tawaf. The Qur’an had told of this promise beforehand in this way,
blocks.7: In fact Allah had shown His Messenger a true dream, which was entirely in accordance with reality. You will surely enter the Masjid al-Haram in safety, in such a state that (some of) you will have your heads shaved and (some) will have hair cut short, without fear. Allah knows what you do not know. So before that dream is fulfilled He has ordained an imminent victory.{{1}}
blocks.8: The dream was true, the timing was Allah’s to set. In between came Khaybar, that imminent victory. A promise that is fulfilled late is not a forgotten promise. In history this ‘umrah is found with four names: Qada’, Qadiyyah, Qisas and Sulh, that is, peace treaty. The treaty about which the Companions had so many questions in their hearts, its very name became one name of this ‘umrah.{{1}}
blocks.10: The three days were completed. Quraysh sent a man to ‘Ali (RA): tell your companion, time is up, let him leave. The Prophet {{1}} set out. From behind a small girl came running, calling, uncle, uncle. Hamzah’s (RA) daughter; her father had been martyred at Uhud, she had stayed behind in Makkah. ‘Ali (RA) took her hand and said to Fatimah (RA), take her, your uncle’s daughter. Then there was a tug-of-war over the girl among three people. ‘Ali (RA) said, I have more right, she is my uncle’s daughter. Ja‘far (RA) said, she is my uncle’s daughter too, and her maternal aunt is my wife. Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) said, she is my brother’s daughter. The Prophet {{2}} gave the girl to her maternal aunt. He said,
blocks.12: A maternal aunt is in the position of a mother. To ‘Ali he said, you are from me and I am from you. To Ja‘far he said, you resemble me in appearance and in character. To Zayd he said, you are our brother, our mawla.{{1}}
blocks.13: Three people quarrelling to keep one orphan girl with them. And in giving the judgement the Prophet {{1}} said to all three such words as they kept in their hearts for life. The ruling went for one, and no one’s heart was broken.
blocks.14: Two of those three that day, Zayd and Ja‘far, would be martyred together on one battlefield only a few months later.
blocks.16: Jumada al-Ula of the eighth year of Hijrah. The Prophet {{1}} had sent al-Harith ibn ‘Umayr al-Azdi (RA) with a letter to the ruler of Busra. On the way near Mu’tah, the Ghassanid ruler loyal to Rome, Shurahbil ibn ‘Amr, bound him and killed him. Killing an envoy was, even in those days, the greatest insult.{{2}}
blocks.17: The Prophet {{1}} sent an army of three thousand. He appointed Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) as commander. He said, if Zayd is martyred then Ja‘far; if Ja‘far is martyred then ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah.{{2}}
blocks.18: On the day of departure everyone gathered to see off the commanders. In that crowd ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) was weeping. The people asked, why are you weeping? He said, by Allah, I am not weeping out of love of the world or love for you. I heard the Prophet {{1}} recite a verse of the Qur’an which says everyone must pass over Hell. I do not know what will happen to me then. The people said, may Allah keep you safe, ward off every danger, bring you back to us victorious. He said,
blocks.20: But I ask the Most Merciful for forgiveness, and ask for a sword-blow that will tear apart the liver and the entrails. Then the traveller will pass by the grave and say, a fighter in the way of Allah, Allah has guided him, he has indeed been guided.{{1}}
blocks.21: Then the army set out. The Prophet {{1}} walked with them as far as Thaniyyat al-Wada‘. Standing there he gave the final farewell.{{2}}
blocks.22: This man is going on, asking for martyrdom, yet his weeping is from fear of accountability. Courage and weeping can be in the same heart. One who does not fear has perhaps not understood anything; one who fears yet goes forward, that one is the brave. Reaching the border of Sham, news came: ahead, a huge army of Rome, with Arab tribes along. Some said, let us write to the Prophet {{1}}, either he will send more men or give other instructions. ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) stood up and said, the very thing you now dislike, martyrdom, is what you came out to seek. We do not fight with numbers or strength; we fight with this religion by which Allah has honoured us. One of the two good things will surely be had: victory, or else martyrdom.{{2}}
blocks.24: The battle began. First of all Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) took up the banner. Sword in hand he fought as few have in all of history. At one point, riddled by the enemy’s spears, he fell; he was martyred. Before the banner could fall to the ground Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib (RA) took it up. He dismounted from his own reddish horse and cut the horse’s legs. He kept fighting. At one point his right hand was cut off and fell. He took the banner in his left hand. A little later the left hand too was gone. Then, pressing the banner between his two arms, he held it high. Thus he was martyred. Then ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) took up the banner. He was on horseback. There was a little hesitation in his heart. He said to himself,
blocks.26: O my nafs! I swear to you, come down onto the battlefield, whether you wish it or not. If others keep the war stirred up and level their spears, why do I see only you sitting away from Paradise?{{1}}
blocks.28: Then he dismounted from the horse. His cousin brought a bone with meat on it and said, brother, strengthen your back with this, a hard day has gone over you today. He took the bone in his hand and bit it once. Then he threw it away and went forward sword in hand. Fighting on, he was martyred. This dialogue with one’s own nafs is familiar to all of us. The heart says, I’ll do this later, let me rest a little now. Ibn Rawahah scolded himself. The bite of the bone was not to satisfy hunger, but to throw off even the thought of how weak the body had grown. Later Ibn ‘Umar (RA) stood by Ja‘far’s body and counted the wounds; fifty blows of spear and sword, not one on the back.{{1}}
blocks.29: When later Ibn ‘Umar (RA) met Ja‘far’s son, he would greet him thus: peace be upon you, O son of the one with two wings.{{1}}
blocks.30: The One Who Gave the News from Madinah
blocks.31: The news from Mu’tah had not yet reached Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} stood before the people and gave the news,
blocks.33: Zayd took the banner, he was martyred. Then Ja‘far took it, he was martyred. Then Ibn Rawahah took it, he was martyred.{{1}}
blocks.34: As he spoke, tears were flowing from his two eyes. Then he said, finally one of the swords of Allah took up the banner, and Allah gave them victory. That sword of Allah was Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA); only a few months earlier he had accepted Islam. He used to say, on the day of Mu’tah nine swords broke in my hand; in the end only a Yemeni broad sword remained in my hand.{{1}}
blocks.35: Thabit ibn Aqram (RA) of Banu ‘Ajlan took up the fallen banner and said, choose one from among yourselves as commander. The people said, you be it. He said, I cannot. Then everyone chose Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA). On the first day, all day, he stood firm before that vast army. He understood that now a strategy was needed by which the Muslims could slowly withdraw from the field, yet the enemy would not get a chance to pursue. If they ran scattered, the Romans would pursue and finish everyone. On the morning of the second day Khalid rearranged the army. He took the front rows to the back, the back rows to the front. The right wing to the left, the left wing to the right. Coming forward, the Romans saw new faces, new banners. They said to one another, help has come to the Muslims from Madinah. A little after the fighting began, Khalid (RA) slowly began to fold the lines and retreat. The army’s discipline was intact. The Romans thought, this is a trap of the Muslims; a strategy to pull them into the desert and finish them. They did not pursue. The Muslim army returned safely to Madinah. Twelve Muslims were martyred in this battle. How many casualties the Romans had is not known. All that is known is that a small band of three thousand returned from before two hundred thousand.{{1}}
blocks.36: Pulling back is sometimes winning. It is because they have the courage to return with everything intact that some are able to stop at the right time. We are afraid to stop, because we count stopping as defeat. After this battle the Arab tribes such as Banu Sulaym, Ashja‘, Ghatafan, Dhubyan and Fazarah, who had been deadly enemies of the Muslims, came one by one and took shelter in the shade of Islam. Mu’tah opened their eyes: those who have this faith with them are not defeated by numbers.{{1}}
blocks.37: Of the three who only a few months earlier had been quarrelling to keep an orphan girl, two of them, and that Ibn Rawahah in whose hand the measure of Khaybar’s crop had been that day, all three went away on one day, on one battlefield. And far away, the one who bade each of them farewell by name, his eyes grew wet.
blocks.38: We think, there is time; I’ll call later, I’ll meet later. The joy the Prophet {{1}} felt at getting Ja‘far back after thirteen years, it took less than a year to lose that same Ja‘far again.
blocks.39: The Three Hundred at the Seashore
blocks.40: Around the time of Mu’tah the Prophet {{1}} sent another small army toward the coast of the sea. Three hundred men, commander Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA). The aim was to block the route of a trade caravan of Quraysh. On the way the food ran low. Abu ‘Ubaydah (RA) told everyone to collect their provisions. Two bags of dates were collected. Every day a little at a time was given to everyone from it. At last a day came when one date per head fell to each. Jabir (RA) was later asked by a student, what can one date do? He said,
blocks.42: When they ran out we felt their lack.{{1}}
blocks.44: Then they reached the edge of the sea. They saw a huge fish lying like a hill. Three hundred men ate from that fish and passed eighteen nights. Abu ‘Ubaydah had two of its ribs set up. A she-camel was saddled and passed under them. It did not touch the ribs. The very army that felt the lack of the date because it had run out, one day got food like a mountain. We often understand the value of a blessing in hand only after losing it. Those who know the price of one date are more thankful for a full meal too. And the army’s commander, the same man, in the days of hunger ate sharing with everyone. He did not keep a separate bag for himself. A leader who shares even the last date with all, people go with him even to the edge of the sea.
blocks.46: From Khaybar to Mu’tah, a few pictures of these year and a half remain in the mind. Ears attentive, waiting for an adhan even on a night of war. The announcement of two rewards for ‘Amir, martyred by his own sword. Ibn Rawahah’s measure, returning the jewellery of the bribe, full justice even with someone he disliked. The poisoned goat and one ‘no’, whose pain he carried for four years. Salamah, who ran alone at Dhu Qarad and brought back all the camels, whom the Prophet {{1}} seated behind him. Bilal, who fell asleep at the time of prayer on the way back, and, with no rebuke, only the next thing to do. The three hundred at the seashore who felt the lack of one date. And Ibn Rawahah’s scolding of his own nafs. The kiss on Ja‘far’s forehead; being unable to decide which was greater, the conquest of Khaybar or the return of a brother. The good news of two hijrahs for the boat people who had been far away. The sweet quarrel of three guardians over Hamzah’s daughter. And the two eyes that grew wet in giving the news of Mu’tah. The brothers with whom one day we walked shoulder to shoulder, they are still there today, but there is no talk. So take away one deed from today’s dars.
blocks.48: When Ja‘far (RA) returned the Prophet {{1}} had said, I cannot tell whether I am happier at the conquest of Khaybar or at Ja‘far’s coming. Today I will ask myself a question: how many brothers in faith were there with whom I no longer speak; is the reason really busyness, or something else? Today I will phone a brother with whom there has been no contact for a long time, and truly want to know how he is; I will not give up this checking in from today.

quiz.q: Why was the instruction to walk fast in the first three rounds given in ‘Umrat al-Qada’?
quiz.e: The polytheists were saying the fever of Yathrib had weakened them.

quiz.q: Who was reciting verses ahead of the Prophet ﷺ in ‘Umrat al-Qada’?
quiz.e: ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA).

quiz.q: To whom did the Prophet ﷺ give Hamzah’s (RA) daughter?
o: He kept her in his own house
quiz.e: A maternal aunt is in the position of a mother.

quiz.q: What is the lesson of ramal, begun in answer to an accusation of weakness, remaining a Sunnah?
o: Walking fast in tawaf is best
Showing the believer’s firmness too becomes worship
quiz.e: A deed of the moment of need became a Sunnah until the Day of Resurrection.

quiz.q: How is Surah al-Fath 48:27 connected to ‘Umrat al-Qada’?
o: The dream was true, the time was set by Allah
The verse was revealed after ‘Umrat al-Qada’
The verse is in fact a direct order for the battle of Khaybar
quiz.e: The dream of Hudaybiyah was fulfilled the next year.

quiz.q: What is the characteristic of the Prophet’s ﷺ ruling in the case of Hamzah’s daughter?
o: He divided her equally among all three
The ruling went for one, and no one’s heart was broken
He returned the girl to Quraysh in Makkah
quiz.e: To all three he said words which they remembered all their lives.

quiz.q: Something you asked of Allah is coming late; what comfort does the incident of ‘Umrat al-Qada’ give?
o: It is better to stop asking
Everything should happen in one’s own time
quiz.e: The dream was true, and it was fulfilled the next year.

quiz.q: Two children are quarrelling and a ruling must go in favour of one; what can be taken from the Prophet’s ﷺ method?
o: Keeping everyone’s heart along with the ruling
Ruling in favour of the elder
Giving no ruling and leaving the matter
quiz.e: To all three he spoke separate words of love.

quiz.q: No one in the family is coming forward to take responsibility for an orphaned relative; which scene of this dars shows the opposite picture?
o: The takbir announcement on the morning of Khaybar
The tug-of-war of three over Hamzah’s daughter
Appointing three commanders in succession for Mu’tah
quiz.e: Three people competing to keep an orphan girl.

quiz.q: In a gathering someone’s verse or speech is shaking the opponent in favour of the religion, yet someone raises an objection; what was the Prophet’s ﷺ position?
o: Silencing the objector and sending him away
Adjourning the gathering and walking out
Letting the speech of good purpose go on
quiz.e: He said, ‘Umar, let him be; his words hit faster than arrows.

quiz.q: Who was the first commander at Mu’tah?
quiz.e: Zayd, then Ja‘far, then Ibn Rawahah.

quiz.q: How many swords broke in Khalid’s (RA) hand on the day of Mu’tah?
quiz.e: Nine; in the end one Yemeni sword remained.

quiz.q: What did Thabit ibn Aqram (RA) do on taking up the fallen banner at Mu’tah?
o: Cut the legs of his own horse
Threw away the bone and took up the sword
Repelled them by throwing stones from the mountain
quiz.e: Everyone chose Khalid; this is Sirah-based.

quiz.q: What is the essence of ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah’s (RA) speech at Mu’tah?
o: To go back and bring more soldiers
To quickly make peace with the enemy
Fighting with the religion, not with numbers
To leave the fight and wait
quiz.e: One of the two good things will surely be had: victory, or else martyrdom.

quiz.q: What is the meaning of none of Ja‘far’s (RA) wounds being on the back?
o: The enemy never got a chance to attack from behind
He did not enter the fight
He did not retreat; he fought from the front
quiz.e: All the wounds were on the front side.

quiz.q: Before the news arrived, the Prophet ﷺ announced the three martyrs; which detail came with it?
o: His two eyes were shedding tears
He told everyone not to leave Madinah
He told them to observe three days of mourning
quiz.e: ‘Wa ‘aynahu tadhrifan’: his two eyes were flowing with water.

quiz.q: Who is meant by ‘one of the swords of Allah’?
quiz.e: The one who finally took up the banner and brought victory.

quiz.q: What does the incident of Ibn Rawahah (RA) scolding his own nafs and descending to the battlefield teach?
o: The right of those far away does not diminish
Justice even with those one dislikes
Not passing judgement by outward appearance
Going against what the heart wants
quiz.e: In the poem he made himself swear and come down.

quiz.q: Seeing a huge obstacle ahead in a task, everyone in the team wants to fall back; what can be taken from Ibn Rawahah’s words?
o: Turning back on seeing an obstacle is wise
Not numbers, but intention and ideal are the strength
First gathering more people is essential
quiz.e: We do not fight with numbers.

quiz.q: Tears come to the eyes while giving news of the death of a loved one; what does the Prophet’s ﷺ practice say?
o: Weeping is a sign of weakness
The news should be given through someone else
Tears are not opposed to patience
quiz.e: His eyes grew wet in giving the news of the three martyrs.

quiz.q: Two of the Companions who had been seen together only a few months earlier were both martyred at Mu’tah; what realisation arises?
o: Going to war should be avoided
Checking on relationships: not later, now
Counting the number of martyrs is necessary
quiz.e: The one I can check on today, perhaps tomorrow I cannot.

quiz.q: Who was the commander of the army of three hundred sent toward the seashore?
quiz.e: Bukhari 4360.

quiz.q: Which is the example of understanding the value of a blessing in hand only after losing it?
o: The martyrdom of three commanders in one day
Feeling the lack of one date
quiz.e: ‘When they ran out we felt it’; Bukhari 4360.

quiz.q: According to the final practical resolve of the dars, what is today’s task?
o: Phoning a brother with whom there has been no talk for a long time
Taking on the responsibility of an orphan
Returning an offer of a bribe
quiz.e: Checking on a brother with whom there is no contact.
